guarantees.claim: When SecSkipPRNGReseeding == 1, unused_force_masks is continuously assigned the value of force_masks_i.
The static lint assertion AesSecSkipPRNGReseedingNonDefault enforces that the parameter SecSkipPRNGReseeding must equal 0; any other value causes a lint error.

assumptions.claim: If the design is configured with SecSkipPRNGReseeding == 1 (overriding the lint assertion), the external input force_masks_i must provide a constant and cryptographically safe mask pattern.
assumptions.risk: An insecure or toggling force_masks_i could create predictable masking values, breaking the AES side-channel protection and potentially enabling key extraction.

uncertain_points.claim: The static lint assertion forces SecSkipPRNGReseeding == 0, yet generate blocks for SecSkipPRNGReseeding == 1 exist. It is ambiguous whether this feature is a test/debug bypass or a supported security-critical configuration.
uncertain_points.risk: If accidentally or maliciously enabled, PRNG reseeding is skipped and arbitrary masks can be forced, likely destroying the randomness that protects AES against side-channel analysis.

uncertain_points.claim: Signal unused_force_masks is explicitly named 'unused' and is assigned only inside the SecSkipPRNGReseeding == 1 block; it may be intentionally dead or only used to suppress lint warnings.
uncertain_points.risk: If truly unused, the signal is harmless but could indicate incomplete design; if inadvertently connected, it could propagate untrusted mask values.
